# Sparse Voxel Storage and Management
Also called: Sparse Voxel Data Structures, SVO Management

## Overview
Sparse Voxel Storage and Management addresses the memory and performance bottlenecks of rendering high-resolution volumetric data by storing only occupied voxels in hierarchical structures (typically octrees) rather than dense grids. It solves the problem of excessive memory bandwidth and storage overhead inherent in naive voxel rendering [S1, S2, unofficial]. Unlike [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md), which processes every voxel in a fixed grid, this family leverages sparsity to skip empty space, enabling real-time rendering of complex scenes that would otherwise exceed VRAM limits.

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental mechanism of converting scalar field data into geometric primitives that are submitted to the graphics pipeline.

1.  **Primitive Generation**: Each occupied voxel is represented by one or more geometric primitives. The most common representation is a cube (6 faces, 24 vertices for flat shading, or 8 vertices for shared shading) or a set of quads representing visible faces [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].
2.  **Coordinate Transformation**: Voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ are transformed into world space. For a dense grid with bounds $P_{min}$ and $P_{max}$ and dimension $N_{dim}$, the world position $P_{world}$ of a voxel center is calculated as [S4, unofficial]:
    $$
    P_{world} = P_{min} + \frac{I_{voxel}}{N_{dim}} \times (P_{max} - P_{min})
    $$
    For unit voxels, this simplifies to $P_{world} = I_{voxel} \times V_{size}$, where $V_{size}$ is the voxel dimension [S2, S4, unofficial].
3.  **Rasterization**: The generated primitives are transformed into clip space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix and rasterized. Visibility is determined by the depth buffer (z-buffer) or a back-to-front painter's algorithm if transparency is required [S2, S3, unofficial].
4.  **Culling**: To manage performance, frustum culling is applied to exclude voxels outside the camera view [S2, S4, unofficial]. Back-face culling is often enabled to discard faces oriented away from the camera, calculated by the dot product of the view-space normal and the view vector [S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Intensity-based Sparse Voxel Storage](1775-intensity-based-sparse-voxel-storage.md)
Eliminates redundant intensity storage by leveraging histogram-based run-length encoding. Choose when memory bandwidth is the primary bottleneck and intensity values are discrete or binned.

### [SVO LOD Management](2990-svo-lod-management.md)
Manages Level of Detail by switching between pre-generated geometric representations (VBOs) at different octree depths. Choose for static, pre-voxelized assets where dynamic generation is too costly.

### [Sparse Voxel Rasterization](3032-sparse-voxel-rasterization.md)
Real-time rasterization of explicit sparse voxels using Morton code sorting and tile-based assignment. Choose for neural radiance field alternatives requiring high fidelity and scalability without ray-casting overhead.

## Background
Sparse voxel techniques emerged as a solution to the memory constraints of dense volume rendering. Early implementations focused on simple intensity-based storage to reduce bandwidth [S1]. Later developments introduced Sparse Voxel Octrees (SVOs) for hierarchical LOD management [S1, unofficial]. Recent advancements integrate sparse voxels into rasterization pipelines using Morton codes for efficient sorting and tile-based rendering, competing with neural implicit representations [S1, S2, unofficial].
